10 Good-Atmosphere Hotels
in Ratchaburi City

heroSub: 10 hand-picked stays in Ratchaburi city that we've reviewed in depth — a European-style hotel with a rooftop pool, a design boutique near the train station, teakwood suites, a hotel with a pool and banquet hall, down to wide rooms in the hundreds of baht with free parking. Prices from about ฿450–1,500/night.
introH2: 🏙️ What kinds of stays does Ratchaburi city have, and how do you pick the right one for your trip?
introHtml: Ratchaburi city is a compact secondary city packed with food and things to do, and most people come on a road trip from Bangkok, about 1.5–2 hours away — what makes choosing a place to stay in town more fun than you'd expect is how many different styles sit within a few kilometres of each other. Some are vintage European-style hotels with a pool and a rooftop breakfast room, some are 6-storey design boutiques where every floor photographs differently and you can walk to the train station, some are teakwood suites or wide serviced apartments in the hundreds of baht. Many people book a stay in town without checking whether it's in the Na Mueang district within walking distance of the market, or over on the Don Tako side near Khao Ngu, which needs a car — only to feel the location doesn't match their plans. This article rounds up 10 stays in Ratchaburi city that we've reviewed in depth, across Na Mueang, Don Tako, Chedi Hak and Ban Rai — every one drawn from reading real guest reviews, telling you both the upsides and the honest caveats, comparing prices across 3 sites, with direct booking links for all.
mrtHtml: Ratchaburi has no metro and no commercial airport, so most people drive from Bangkok, about 1.5–2 hours along Phetkasem Road, or take a southern-line train / minivan into the city. The stays in this article are spread across 4 districts of Mueang Ratchaburi, so you can choose by your plans: Na Mueang — the city centre, near the market, Wat Mahathat, Robinson and the train station, somewhat walkable (S.Swiss, Happy Home, Veerasuda) · downtown along Thao U Thong Road — about 500 m walk to the train station (Space 59) · Don Tako — the quiet western suburb near Khao Kaen Chan and Khao Ngu Stone Park, needs a car (Navela, Tai-Shan, The Sun) · Chedi Hak / Ban Rai — the city edge along Phetkasem Road, easy to drive to (Western Grand, Tulip Place, Baan Lamoon). Almost all have free parking, which suits self-drivers best.

entries.name: S.Swiss Hotel Ratchaburi
entries.revCount: Traveloka 8.7 · 207 reviews · TripAdvisor #2 specialty lodging in Ratchaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Mueang · ~2 km from Wat Mahathat
entries.addr: 18 Soi Maen Ramluek, Na Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: Among the stays in central Ratchaburi, if you want somewhere with more "design flair" than a plain pass-through bedroom, many reviews put S.Swiss Hotel near the top of the list. It's a 4-star city hotel, an 8-storey building with 77 rooms, that plays with a vintage European theme from the facade right through to the interiors, set in the Na Mueang district about 2 km from Wat Mahathat Worawihan and the city market. The most-mentioned feature, and what sets it apart from a typical city hotel, is the open-air rooftop pool and breakfast room — a white-tiled pool against the blue of the water, an airy spot that catches the morning breeze, where families and couples like to head up. Honest takes from real reviews on Traveloka, Agoda and TripAdvisor agree strongly that the rooms are spacious, clean, with comfortable beds and decor that punches above the price; many say it feels like staying in a small hotel in Europe, the cleanliness category scores up to around 9.0, and the room rate still includes a buffet breakfast with a fresh-made omelette corner. Free parking holds around 80 cars, so self-drivers can relax about a spot. Honest caveats from the reviews: there's no main restaurant or in-house bar, so lunch and dinner mean heading out, the rooms have no tea/coffee kettle, the TV only has Thai channels, and a few rooms have Japanese toilet or aircon issues worth checking at check-in. The area around the hotel is residential and commercial rather than a walking district, so it suits self-drivers more. In short, if you want to stay in central Ratchaburi somewhere with style, a wide clean room and a pool, at a 4-star price that's still within reach, this delivers on that well enough to rank among the top stays in town.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Use the rooftop pool and breakfast room in the morning or late morning, when the sun loungers are freer than in the evening. Bring your own coffee or tea sachets since the rooms have no kettle, and line up a place in town for lunch and dinner since the hotel has no in-house restaurant.
pros: Open-air rooftop pool and breakfast room with good atmosphere
Wide, clean rooms with vintage European decor that punches above the price (cleanliness around 9.0)
Rate includes buffet breakfast with a fresh-made omelette corner
Central location, free parking for around 80 cars
cons: No in-house restaurant or bar, lunch and dinner mean heading out
No tea/coffee kettle in the rooms, and the TV only has Thai channels
The area around the hotel isn't a walking district, better with a car (per reviews)

entries.name: Navela Hotel & Banquet (Na Vela)
entries.revCount: Trip.com 9.0 · TripAdvisor 4.3/5 · 39 reviews · #2 guesthouse/inn in Ratchaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Don Tako · ~10 min drive to the city
entries.addr: 9/9 Moo 5, Don Tako Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a stay in Ratchaburi city with new, clean rooms, a pool, and a reasonable price for a weekend family trip, Navela Hotel & Banquet (Thai name "Na Vela") is a name that comes up often in reviews. It's a 4-star hotel of around 45 rooms in Don Tako sub-district that combines the roles of "a place to stay" and "a banquet centre" — part guest rooms, part ballroom, meeting rooms and a wedding/seminar banquet hall (the source of the Banquet in its name), done in a warm contemporary Thai style. What real reviews mention again and again is the newness and cleanliness of the rooms — many say the rooms look new, with modern furniture and bathrooms, comfortable beds, and some rooms have a balcony for sitting out over a garden or pool view. The highlight families with kids love most is the outdoor pool with sun loungers, which looks cleaner and better laid out than you'd expect at this price, alongside a gym and a tidy, spacious garden. There's an in-house restaurant the reviews praise for tasty Thai food at friendly prices, and broad free parking. TripAdvisor ranks it #2 of 23 guesthouse/inn-type stays in Ratchaburi. Honest caveats from the reviews: the Don Tako side has no shops within walking distance, so you should have a car; some rooms have no safe or tea/coffee set, and some items cost extra, such as an extra towel; breakfast choices may be limited for international guests, and on big banquet days the atmosphere is livelier than usual — if you want quiet, check ahead and ask for a top-floor room. In short, if you want clean new rooms, a pool and easy parking for around a thousand-plus baht for a Ratchaburi road trip, Navela is good value and does this well.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose a room with a balcony — a few hundred baht more than a standard Superior gets you a seat out over a garden or pool view. Bring your own toiletries like a toothbrush, and check with the hotel whether there's a banquet/seminar during your stay; if you want quiet, ask for a top-floor room.
pros: New rooms, very clean, modern furniture and bathrooms, comfortable beds
Clean outdoor pool, good for kids to swim, plus a gym and spacious garden
Tasty in-house Thai restaurant at friendly prices · broad free parking
Good value at around a thousand-plus baht · TripAdvisor #2 guesthouse/inn in Ratchaburi
cons: The Don Tako side has no shops within walking distance, you should have a car
Some rooms have no safe / tea/coffee set, and some items cost extra
On banquet/seminar days the atmosphere is livelier than usual (per reviews)

entries.name: Space 59 Hotel
entries.badge: 📸 Every floor photographs · Near the train station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Thao U Thong Road · ~500 m from the train station
tags: 🚆 ~500 m walk to the train station
entries.addr: 8/9 Thao U Thong Road, Na Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you think a budget stay in a provincial city centre has to mean a plain, ordinary room, Space 59 Hotel will likely change your mind. It's a 6-storey boutique hotel in central Ratchaburi on Thao U Thong Road, deliberately done in a raw, cool loft style, and what reviewers mention most is that each floor is decorated with a different concept, from raw exposed concrete to woodwork to loft-style corners, until reviewers habitually call it photogenic at almost every angle. The location is the first strong point, since it's only about 500 m from Ratchaburi train station, walkable if your luggage isn't heavy — ideal for those who take the southern-line train straight into Ratchaburi and don't drive. There are several room types, from a standard Superior, to a two-storey Duplex with high ceilings, a sitting area below and a loft bed above (the type couples and photo lovers book most), up to a family Suite with a small kitchen. Reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com, Wongnai and TripAdvisor agree that the rooms are clean, beds comfortable, and they look just like the photos, especially for the price you pay, with the value-for-money score up to around 9.4. A small highlight that makes it feel like more than you paid for is free coffee, Ovaltine and toast all day, alongside free bikes to borrow and free parking. Honest caveats: the walls don't soundproof very well, so you hear the neighbours a bit; breakfast is fairly limited (sometimes a single plate each, not a buffet); some rooms have no hairdryer, so you borrow one from the front desk; and if you arrive late after midnight the in-building parking may be full, leaving you to park on the street. In short, if you want a stylish, photogenic room downtown on a budget, within walking distance of the train station, this is good value and steadily recommended.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose the two-storey Duplex if you want a nice corner, and some have a balcony with a city view. If you're a light sleeper, ask for a corner room or a quieter floor and bring earplugs, since the walls don't soundproof very well. If you're driving and expect to arrive late, call the hotel ahead about parking.
pros: Each floor has different decor, photogenic at every angle, photo lovers approve
Downtown location, about 500 m walk to the train station and market
Free coffee, Ovaltine and toast all day · free bikes and parking
Clean rooms, just like the photos, great value (value-for-money around 9.4)
cons: The walls don't soundproof very well, you hear the neighbours a bit
Breakfast is fairly limited, not a buffet · some rooms have no hairdryer
Arrive late and the in-building parking may be full, leaving street parking (per reviews)

entries.name: Western Grand Hotel Ratchaburi
entries.badge: 🅿️ Parking + EV charger · Banquet hall for 700
entries.addr: 105/1 Old Phetkasem Road, Na Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a stay in Ratchaburi city that's easy to drive to, easy to park at, and not expensive, for a short trip or running errands, Western Grand Hotel Ratchaburi is a name locals have known for a long time. It's a 4-star city hotel of 76 rooms on Phetkasem Road, open since 2006 with a major renovation in 2018, and its stance is clear: a hometown hotel of the practical, "real-use" kind, leaning on convenience and value over luxury. The main strength is the Phetkasem Road location, easy to get in and out of from both the Bangkok and Phetchaburi sides, a few minutes' drive to the old Koh Yeekee market, temples and museums. What many people especially like is the spacious free parking with an electric-vehicle (EV) charger, which matters a lot for self-drivers, with no circling for a spot. There's an outdoor pool, gym, massage room and the Ratchaphruek restaurant serving Thai-international food, and the breakfast buffet is a point several international reviews praise as varied and good value. What makes it known in the province is its large banquet and seminar halls, led by the Kanlapaphruek ballroom that holds up to 700. On the praise side, reviews say the rooms are clean, beds comfortable, staff friendly, and it's good value. Honest caveats: as a building open since 2006, some rooms and the decor are starting to show their age despite the 2018 renovation; Wi-Fi is sometimes slow or unstable; some rooms' aircon doesn't cool fully; Phetkasem Road out front has traffic all the time, so rooms facing the road hear some noise; and some days are lively because of banquet events. In short, if you want a city base that's easy to reach, easy to park at, with full amenities for 1–2 nights on a reachable budget, Western Grand does that job well.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Ask for a room not facing Phetkasem Road and choose Deluxe or above for a better room than the cheapest standard. If you really need to work, pack a mobile data SIM as a backup since Wi-Fi can be slow at times, and check ahead whether there's a banquet event during your stay.
pros: Spacious free parking with an EV charger, good for self-drivers
City-centre location on Phetkasem Road, easy access, near the market and temples
Has a pool, gym, massage room and a varied breakfast buffet
Large banquet hall for 700 · friendly staff, clean rooms, good value
cons: The building and some of the decor are aged (open since 2006)
Wi-Fi is sometimes slow/unstable · some rooms' aircon doesn't cool fully
Rooms facing the road hear traffic · some days are lively from banquet events

entries.name: Tai-Shan Suites
entries.revCount: Trip.com 8.6 · 31 reviews · TripAdvisor 4.4/5 · #4 B&B/Inn in Ratchaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Don Tako · Quiet, off the main road
entries.addr: 278 Moo 10, Don Tako Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're planning to stop in Ratchaburi for a night and don't want to pay a lot, but also don't want the small, cramped room of a typical budget hotel, Tai-Shan Suites is a name reviewers mention often among this city's stays in the hundreds of baht. What sets it apart is that the word "suite" in the name isn't just marketing, because several room types are noticeably wider than the price you pay, and some genuinely separate the sitting zone from the bed zone, making it feel more like staying in a small apartment than a typical hotel room. Open since 2015, the building is around 7 storeys with about 78 rooms, in Don Tako sub-district about 1.5 km from the district office. What reviews agree on is the warm-toned teakwood throughout — the doors, wardrobes and parquet floors — that makes the rooms feel cosy and look pricier than they are; the bathroom is glass-partitioned into dry and wet zones, clean, looks new, and the water pressure is fine. The most repeated praise is the cleanliness and the room size relative to the price, with many saying it feels like getting a condo unit rather than a hotel room. Another much-praised point is the free covered parking with CCTV and a security guard — self-drivers rate the car's security highly — and the location on a soi that's off the main road, so it's quiet and you sleep well. Honest caveats: there's no pool or leisure-type amenities; the Don Tako location is far from the main tourist areas and fairly car-dependent; breakfast is simple with few choices; some furniture is starting to age with the building's years; and a few rooms have a slight musty smell when first opened, which clears once the aircon ventilates. In short, if you want a wide, clean, budget room with free parking, especially as a self-driver, this is good value and hard to match in its class on room size.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Choose the Suite group with a separate sitting zone — the price difference is small but you get clearly more space. Self-driving makes the most sense since the location is far from the tourist areas, and you get to use the free covered parking. If you're sensitive to smells, run the aircon to ventilate for a while after entering the room.
pros: Suite-style rooms wider than the price, several separate the sitting zone from the bed
Warm-toned teakwood feels cosy · clean rooms and bathrooms
Free covered parking with CCTV and a guard, secure
Quiet because it's off the main road, you sleep well · from just around ฿638
cons: No pool or leisure-type amenities
The Don Tako location is far from the main tourist areas, you should have a car
Simple breakfast with few choices · some furniture is starting to age

entries.name: Baan Lamoon
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Ban Rai · ~2-3 km from the city
tags: 💰 One of the cheapest in the city
entries.addr: 88 Moo 2, Ban Rai Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after the lightest possible price for a Ratchaburi stay but still want a room that's clean, wide and genuinely comfortable to sleep in, Baan Lamoon is the name budget travellers mention most in Ratchaburi city. It's a serviced apartment in Ban Rai sub-district that acts as a nightly stay in the hundreds of baht, but gives you a room of around 26 square metres with a balcony, sofa, fridge and cold aircon, wider than many places at the same price. The main room comes in two versions on the same layout, differing in the bed: Superior King with one large bed, and Superior Twin with two single beds. What reviews mention most is that the rooms are wide and not cramped, unlike typical cheap rooms, and having a fridge and sofa makes it feel more like a rental than a hotel room, good for those staying several nights. Honest takes from real reviews on Trip.com, Agoda and Booking.com especially praise the comfortable beds, strong bathroom water pressure and icy-cold aircon — the three things budget-stay guests weigh most — with the value-for-money score up to around 9.2. A point that surprises many is that it has a gym to use for free, rare in a stay in the hundreds of baht, plus a wide free private parking lot. Honest caveats: this isn't a resort or photogenic boutique, with no pool, restaurant or breakfast; soundproofing is incomplete, so you hear some noise from the corridor and neighbouring rooms; the entrance at night looks quiet and a bit dim; and it's about 2-3 km outside the city, so you should have a car. In short, for budget travellers, workers, drivers passing through, or families who just want a value sleeping base, this fits just right, and the real review score still holds at around 8.8.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you're a light sleeper, bring earplugs and try asking for a top-floor room or a corner away from the main corridor, since soundproofing is incomplete. There's no restaurant or breakfast, so if you arrive late, buy some food to keep in the fridge. Self-driving is most convenient since it's about 2-3 km outside the city.
pros: Wide 26 sqm rooms with a balcony, fridge and sofa, beyond the hundreds-of-baht price
Comfortable beds, strong water pressure, good cold aircon (value-for-money around 9.2)
A gym to use for free, which is rare at this price
Wide free private parking · one of the cheapest in the city
cons: Soundproofing is incomplete, you hear the corridor and neighbouring rooms
No pool, restaurant or breakfast
About 2-3 km outside the city, the entrance is quiet at night, you should have a car

entries.name: The Sun Resort Ratchaburi
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Don Tako · ~2.2 km from Khao Wang
entries.addr: 238 Moo 5, Don Tako Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a Ratchaburi stay that's cheap, cutely designed, and has free parking, for a night or two before heading out to make merit at temples, see the dragon jars, or stop by Khao Ngu Stone Park, The Sun Resort Ratchaburi is a small boutique resort that opened in 2021 in Don Tako sub-district, on the western edge of town. It's a small resort of around 37 rooms with a clear stance: rooms decorated in a loft style and themed rooms that look better than the price, with a garden and small terrace to sit out. What people mention most is the loft-style themed rooms that look more designed than the price — many play with exposed-concrete walls, wooden furniture, warm-toned lighting and photogenic corners — ranging from a Basic large-bed room, Standard and Superior king rooms, twin rooms with a mountain view, up to an 8-bed dorm for groups of friends or backpackers priced lower still per bed. On the praise side, reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor agree that the rooms are clean, cutely decorated, beds comfortable, and the Wi-Fi is fast enough for work calls, with free coffee and drinking water in the room, free private parking near the room, and free bikes to borrow — many even say they got a lovely room at an unbelievably cheap price. Honest caveats: it's a small resort with no pool and no gym; upkeep of the themed rooms is uneven in places, such as mismatched bulb colours, a damaged bathtub, few power outlets, and some small rooms have no window. The location needs a car since the restaurants around aren't within walking distance, and the breakfast terms differ across platforms, so check clearly when booking. In short, if you want a cute room at a light price, free parking and a quiet atmosphere for sleeping between sights around Ratchaburi, this is impressively good value for budget travellers.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you want light and a view, choose a mountain-view twin room or Superior and above, since some small rooms have no window. Pack a power strip since some rooms have few outlets, and check the breakfast terms clearly when booking, as the information differs across platforms.
pros: Photogenic loft-style themed rooms that look more designed than the hundreds-of-baht price
Has a budget 8-bed dorm, good for groups of friends and backpackers
Fast Wi-Fi for work · free parking and bikes to borrow
Quiet atmosphere, very good value at a hundreds-of-baht price
cons: No pool and no gym · a small resort that just opened in 2021
Upkeep of the themed rooms is uneven in places · some rooms have no window / few outlets
The location needs a car, the restaurants around aren't within walking distance (per reviews)

entries.name: Happy Home Hotel Ratchaburi
entries.badge: ✨ High score 9.1 · Near the train station
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Na Mueang · ~1 km from the train station
tags: 🛏️ Every room has a private balcony
🅿️ Free parking · near the train station
entries.addr: 8 Soi Maen Ramluek 4, Na Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a stay in Ratchaburi city that's very light on price, with clean rooms and easy parking, for a night or two before heading out, Happy Home Hotel Ratchaburi is a name budget travellers talk about a lot. It's a 3-star city hotel of 71 rooms on Soi Maen Ramluek 4 in the Na Mueang area that clearly plays the role of "a budget stay that's clean and quiet." The main strength is the in-city location that's only about 1 km from Ratchaburi train station and about 0.5 km from the provincial hall, so those who come by train can comfortably walk or take a short ride, while Wat Mahathat, the museum and the old market are a 5–10 minute drive away. A point many reviews agree on is that every room has a private balcony, which isn't common at this price, and every room has aircon, a fridge, cable TV and an en-suite bathroom with hot water. Honest takes from real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor align strongly on the praise side that the rooms are spotlessly clean, wider than expected, beds comfortable, the fridge is large, and there are plenty of charging outlets, good for longer stays — the cleanliness and service categories score up to around 9.2, and staff are praised as polite and friendly, pushing the overall score up to around 9.1, surprisingly high for a hundreds-of-baht price. Free parking for both cars and motorcycles. Honest caveats: the in-room Wi-Fi signal is weak in spots, the walls are fairly thin and don't soundproof well, and the mattress is fairly firm for some; there's no pool or buffet breakfast (breakfast is à la carte, sometimes charged separately); and the soi it sits on is fairly quiet, not by a restaurant area. There's a deposit of around ฿300 at check-in, refunded at checkout. In short, if you want a city-centre stay that's clean, quiet, easy to park at and as budget as possible, Happy Home does that job beyond its price.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Have a deposit of around ฿300 ready at check-in (refunded at checkout) so it's no surprise. If you're sensitive to noise, choose the wider Deluxe and ask for a room at the end of the corridor since the walls are fairly thin. Pack a mobile data SIM as a backup since the in-room Wi-Fi is weak in spots, and line up a place in town for lunch and dinner.
pros: Spotlessly clean rooms, wide enough for longer stays (cleanliness/service around 9.2)
Every room has a private balcony, a large fridge, plenty of charging outlets
Free parking, city-centre, about 1 km from the train station
Polite, friendly staff · from just ฿546, value beyond expectations
cons: No pool or buffet breakfast (breakfast à la carte, charged separately)
In-room Wi-Fi weak in spots · walls fairly thin · mattress firm for some
The soi it sits on is quiet, not by a restaurant area · deposit of around ฿300

entries.name: Tulip Place Ratchaburi
entries.badge: 🅿️ Free covered parking · Near Khao Kaen Chan
entries.mrtTag: 📍 Chedi Hak · ~5 min to Khao Kaen Chan
tags: 🛏️ Clean rooms, comfy beds beyond the price
🛣️ Along Phetkasem Road, easy to drive to
entries.addr: 80/2 Phetkasem Road, Chedi Hak Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a Ratchaburi stay that's simple, clean, light on price and easy to drive to, for a single overnight on the way, or as a base before heading out to Khao Kaen Chan and the city, Tulip Place Ratchaburi is a name drivers along Phetkasem Road know by sight. It's a small serviced-apartment-style 3-star stay, open since around 2016, along Phetkasem Road (Highway 4) in Chedi Hak sub-district on the city edge, with only a few dozen rooms, so it feels quieter and more private than a big hotel. The location is both a strength and something to understand: it's along Phetkasem Road, very easy to drive in and out of from both the Bangkok and Phetchaburi sides, and in the same zone as Khao Kaen Chan, the city's viewpoint and Buddha image, a few minutes' drive away, while the city and train station are about 7 km off. The most-mentioned standout is the free covered private parking for around 30 cars, close to the rooms, so the car isn't out in the sun and rain. Honest takes from real reviews on Trip.com, TripAdvisor and other platforms agree on the praise side that the rooms are clean, beds comfortable, the aircon cools well, and the bathroom water pressure is good — a point many find a pleasant surprise relative to the price — and staff are friendly and good at recommending local eateries. Honest caveats: it's a small budget stay with no pool, no lift and no breakfast; room soundproofing isn't great, so you hear some noise from neighbouring rooms or the road; the Wi-Fi signal is uneven at times; and the decor and bathroom are a slightly older style with the building's age. In short, for self-drivers who want a clean sleep, comfy bed, free covered parking and the most budget price in Ratchaburi for a single overnight, Tulip Place does its job well in the way a budget stay should.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: If you have a lot of luggage or are travelling with elderly companions, ask for a ground-floor room when booking, since there's no lift. If you're sensitive to noise, ask for an interior corner room not facing the road, and choose Deluxe or above for more space and a better room than Standard. Pack a mobile data SIM as a backup since the Wi-Fi is unstable at times.
pros: Free covered parking for around 30 cars, parked close to the room
Clean rooms, comfortable beds, good cold aircon, good water pressure, beyond the price
Along Phetkasem Road, easy to drive to, about 5 min to Khao Kaen Chan
Very budget price, good value for a single overnight
cons: No pool, no lift and no breakfast
Room soundproofing isn't great, you hear some outside noise
Uneven Wi-Fi signal · not in the city centre, dinner within walking distance isn't convenient

entries.name: Veerasuda Condotel
entries.badge: 🪵 Wide teakwood rooms · Walk to Robinson

rooms.type: Twin Room (~30 sqm, two separate beds)

tags: 🏙️ Walk to Robinson and the old market
entries.addr: 20/30-37 Soi 1, Somboonkul Road, Na Mueang Sub-district, Mueang Ratchaburi District
entries.storyHtml: If you're after a stay in Ratchaburi city that's light on price but gives you a proper private room — not a small-bed guesthouse in a cramped room — Veerasuda Condotel is a 3-star serviced apartment right in the city centre, in the Na Mueang area. The building is around 5 storeys with about 90–100 rooms; the word condotel means you get an apartment-style room with a fridge, hot-water system and living space like a real home, not just a pass-through bedroom. What sets it apart from a typical budget stay is the decor in teakwood furniture — the bed, wardrobe and table — making the rooms feel warmer and more substantial than typical board-furniture rooms. The biggest strength is the city-centre location that walks comfortably to Robinson Ratchaburi at about 0.5 km, and the museum and old Koh Yeekee market at about 0.9 km, with the location category scoring up to around 8.4, its best category. Honest takes from real reviews on Traveloka, Agoda and TripAdvisor agree that the rooms are wide at around 30 square metres and cleaner than the price — many say they got a bigger-than-expected room at this price level — staff are friendly and helpful, and there's free parking, a lift, key cards, CCTV and 24-hour security. It takes both daily and monthly stays, good for those working in the city for several days. Honest caveats: the rate doesn't include breakfast, and the in-house food is the weakest point (scoring around 5.5); as a long-open building, some items in the rooms are starting to age; the actual room you get may differ from the website photos, or a better room costs extra; and there's no pool or gym. In short, if you want a wide, clean private room downtown on a budget, or are looking for a monthly stay, Veerasuda is good value in its price range.
entries.tipHtml: 💡 Tip: Confirm the room type and booking details clearly before arriving, since some reviews report misunderstandings at check-in, and try asking to view the room or to get one that's just been serviced, as it's a long-open building. The rate doesn't include breakfast, so plan breakfast at the eateries around or at the nearby Robinson. For longer stays, ask about the monthly rate directly.

faqTitle: FAQ — Common traveller questions about stays in Ratchaburi city

faq.q: ❓ What's the best stay in Ratchaburi city?
faq.a: It depends on your trip style and budget. If you measure by review score, Space 59 Hotel scores 9.2, a design boutique near the train station, and Happy Home Hotel scores 9.1, clean and wide at the highest hundreds-of-baht score in this article. If you want a pool, S.Swiss Hotel has a rooftop pool with breakfast included, or Navela has an outdoor pool and new rooms. If you focus on a wide room at a light price, Baan Lamoon at ฿450 with 26 sqm rooms. If you want a suite, Tai-Shan Suites with a separate teakwood sitting zone.

faq.q: ❓ How much do stays in Ratchaburi city cost?
faq.a: In this article, prices start at around ฿450–1,500 per night. The most budget side is Baan Lamoon from ฿450, Happy Home ฿546, The Sun Resort and Tulip Place ฿550. The mid range is Veerasuda ฿600, Tai-Shan ฿638, Space 59 ฿700, Western Grand ฿900. And the upper level is S.Swiss ฿1,260 and Navela ฿1,500. All prices are approximate starting prices from the standard room; over long holidays and festivals prices may be higher than usual.

faq.q: ❓ Which area is good to stay in Ratchaburi city?
faq.a: Na Mueang (the city centre, near the market, temples, Robinson and the train station, somewhat walkable) — S.Swiss, Happy Home, Veerasuda · downtown along Thao U Thong Road (about 500 m walk to the train station) — Space 59 · Don Tako (the western suburb, quiet, near Khao Kaen Chan and Khao Ngu Stone Park, needs a car) — Navela, Tai-Shan, The Sun · Chedi Hak / Ban Rai (the city edge along Phetkasem Road, easy to drive to) — Western Grand, Tulip Place, Baan Lamoon

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in Ratchaburi city have a pool?
faq.a: In this article, 3 places have a pool. S.Swiss Hotel ฿1,260, an open-air rooftop pool and breakfast room, breakfast included · Navela Hotel & Banquet ฿1,500, an outdoor pool with sun loungers and a gym, good for kids to swim · and Western Grand Hotel ฿900, with an outdoor pool, gym and massage room. Most of the other budget stays in this article are city hotels or serviced apartments without a pool.

faq.q: ❓ Which stays in Ratchaburi city suit people without a car?
faq.a: Without a car, choose the Na Mueang or downtown area within walking distance of the market and train station. Space 59 Hotel is about 500 m from the train station and walks to the market and restaurants · Happy Home Hotel is about 1 km from the train station and the provincial hall · Veerasuda Condotel walks to Robinson and the old market · while stays on the Don Tako side (Navela, Tai-Shan, The Sun), Chedi Hak and Ban Rai (Western Grand, Tulip Place, Baan Lamoon) are fairly car-dependent since the shops aren't within walking distance.

faq.q: ❓ How far ahead should I book a stay in Ratchaburi city?
faq.a: Most are small to mid-sized stays (24–127 reviews, some only a few dozen rooms); on normal weekdays, booking 1–2 weeks ahead is enough. But over long holidays, festivals and the travel season (late rains to cool season) you should book several weeks ahead, especially nice rooms like Space 59's Duplex and high-scoring stays like Happy Home and Navela that fill fast. Every platform has Free Cancellation, so we recommend locking in that kind of rate first if your plans aren't set, then comparing Agoda / Booking / Trip.com for the best price.
